//: Lighthouse CI budgets for the SEO audit workflow (.github/workflows/seo-audit.yml).
JSON has no comment syntax and LHCI parses this file with a plain JSON.parse, so this key
carries the notes instead. It sits beside `ci`, not inside it, and is ignored by the loader.
THESE THRESHOLDS WERE SET WITH NO BACKEND RUNNING, and they are measurements rather than
guesses. The workflow starts the Next.js production build alone and points API_INTERNAL_URL
at a dead port, so every server-side read fails and the pages render their offline
fallbacks. Measured on 2026-09-14 against that exact setup, 3 runs per URL, Lighthouse
12.6.1: the four gated URLs each scored SEO 1.00 and Accessibility 1.00 on every run, with
no variance; best-practices 0.96; performance 0.86 to 0.97.
SEO is therefore gated at 1.0, not at a round 0.9. Its audits are deterministic markup
checks, so the observed variance is zero, and a 0.9 line would have left enough headroom
for a lost canonical or a stray noindex to pass unnoticed -- the exact regression this
workflow exists to catch. Accessibility keeps a little room at 0.95 because a few of its
audits (contrast, tap targets) depend on rendering rather than markup. Performance is
observed, never enforced: its number describes the offline fallback on runner hardware.
WHY /en/destinations/tokyo IS NOT LISTED, although the task asked for it: the guide page
throws on purpose when the destination catalog cannot be read (an outage has to be a 5xx,
since a 404 invites Google to drop a real page), and loadDestinations() also returns null
for an empty catalog. Without seeded destination rows the URL is a hard 500, and the
action's collect loop aborts the whole run on a failed document -- so including it would
destroy collection for the other four URLs rather than merely score badly.
/zh-TW/destinations stands in: it degrades identically and adds second-locale coverage.
To restore the city guide once this job runs against a seeded API, add it to collect.url
AND to a matching assertMatrix pattern. A URL that matches no pattern is collected and
then asserted against nothing, silently, which looks exactly like passing.
/en/hotspots is collected but only warned on. Without the API it renders a short
'unavailable' card carrying noindex by design; that single is-crawlable audit is the whole
of its measured SEO 0.66, so a hard gate there would encode the outage as the expectation.
ci.upload below is ignored by treosh/lighthouse-ci-action, which runs its own filesystem
upload without passing --config. It is kept so that a local `lhci autorun --config=` writes
reports somewhere useful instead of defaulting to target 'lhci' and failing.
